comparator.academicYear: Current prospective curriculum pages checked 2026-09-25 (concurrent year overviews)
comparator.route: General Politicologie bachelor with open third-year choice
comparator.sourceNotes: The official prospective year pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Years one and two each list ten 6-EC compulsory political-science courses, including methods, statistics, two second-year projects and international/conflict study. Year three lists 6 EC Politics, Ethics and Practice, 6 EC International Relations in the Indo-Pacific, one 6-EC choice between democracy-under-pressure and borders/migration options, 30 EC genuine minor/elective/internship space and a required 12-EC bachelor thesis. The year-two page spells “Qualtitative”; the source name is retained verbatim in the comparator. Third-year named electives and thesis themes are choices, not all compulsory. Prospectus year pages show concurrent cohorts and are not a guarantee of a single entrant-cohort three-year timetable.

alternatives.label: Political institutions, democracy and social change
alternatives.concept: A broad political-science response through comparative politics, political philosophy, European governance, social inequality, movements, international relations, peace and conflict, and empirical research. UCR integrates related courses from several disciplines but does not reproduce Radboud’s dedicated political-science methods projects or thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The scheduled sequence visibly covers domestic and comparative institutions, European politics, movements, methods and political ethics.
progression: All 24 courses are scheduled for their terms; formal prerequisites precede their dependent courses and at least six courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: International relations, conflict and peace
alternatives.concept: A second UCR route retains comparative politics and political methods while shifting its upper-level emphasis to international relations, war, conflict transformation, human rights, foreign-policy ethics and political violence. It does not replicate Radboud’s advanced Indo-Pacific case or political-science research projects.
alternatives.labelReason: The scheduled peace, conflict, war, law and political-violence coursework makes this a sustained international focus.
progression: All 24 courses are scheduled for their terms; formal prerequisites precede their dependent courses and at least six courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces several domestic-politics, constitutional-law and social-psychology courses with war history, political violence, criminal justice and international ethics; it differs from the closest match by more than four courses (30 EC).

routeSelection.route: General Politicologie bachelor with open third-year choice
routeSelection.basis: The target is the ordinary degree without a named specialization. The 6-EC advanced choice and 30-EC free space remain open, rather than fixing an elective, minor or internship.

selection.assessment: Two distinct feasible UCR pathways cover the broad political-science core and an international-conflict focus. A third democracy, social justice or political-theory proposal would mostly rearrange the same small UCR politics, law and sociology catalogue and lacks four course changes backed by a distinct political-science sequence.

notes.text: UCR offers substantive comparative politics, political theory, international relations, peace and conflict, EU law, sociology and cross-disciplinary research methods. Radboud requires a denser political-science methods curriculum, two project courses and a 12-EC discipline-specific thesis. UCR alternatives illustrate related programmes, without implying equivalent credits, political-science qualification or admission guarantees.
